newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Investor posts jump in 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Investor posts jump in 1996 profits.

text.p: Swedish investment company Investor AB, the key holding company in the Wallenberg family's financial empire, said Thursday its pre-tax profits more than tripled in 1996.
Its pre-tax profit soared to 9.60 billion crowns ($1.3 billion) from 3.05 billion ($409.3 million) a year earlier.
Company President Claes Dahlback called 1996 one of the best years ever.
"For Investor, 1996 was a very good year, one of the best in our 80 year history," Dahlback said in the statement.
Investor, whose largest holding by value is Swedish drug company AB Astra, said it would pay out a dividend of 10 crowns per share ($1.35) compared with nine crowns ($1.21) last year.
The earnings statement also showed a 3.48 billion crown ($466.9 million) cash injection for Saab Automobile AB, which Investor owns jointly with General Motors/Opel.
